sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Candidate faithfully encodes ice-class applicability, required evidence, metre-valued decimal draughts, and inclusive lower/upper bounds for fore and aft draughts.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Refactor the large nested-OPTIONAL cross-product query into conditional SHACL Core constraints plus one bounded comparison query. Keep applicability limited to iceClassIaSuper, iceClassIa, iceClassIb, and iceClassIc; in the applicable branch, use Core property/node constraints to require the upper and lower waterlines and all fore/aft operating and waterline QuantityValues, with xsd:decimal numeric values and unit:M. Use a compact SPARQL constraint only to report lower > operating or operating > upper at either perpendicular. Remove the invented isIRI requirements for waterline nodes, since valid range instances may be blank nodes and the verified requirement does not require IRIs.

Do not let a missing, unknown, or conflicting iceClass satisfy the non-applicable branch. Require exactly one nltl:iceClass value, restrict it to the six supplied controlled values, and encode non-applicability explicitly for nltl:iceClassIi or nltl:iceClassIii; apply the draught constraints explicitly for IA Super, IA, IB, or IC. This prevents unknown applicability evidence from passing. Also make singular waterlines, draught quantities, numeric values, and units maxCount 1, and express the fore/aft comparisons as explicit bounded branches rather than predicate-variable combinatorial joins.
Candidate faithfully encodes ice-class applicability, required evidence, metre-valued decimal draughts, and inclusive lower/upper bounds for fore and aft draughts.
